Alright. I can see your point. Personally, I see it the other way.

"The perfect fantasy Goddess. She literally needs to be objectified by men, much like a centerfold, in order to function. And at the same time she remains untouched and pure. The best of both worlds."

I would say it is exactly the opossite of anti-feminism here. She is a goddess of fertility, so the sexual part of this SCP is integral, it shouldn't offend on it's own. And as you said, she is pure. She is being objectified because that is how it works. There are many SCPs that make you read about things that are morally wrong but I would say that this is not one of them. If anything, it is the men in this article that are feeling ashamed of doing what they have to do. She doesn't seem to mind. And that isn't any proof of being brainwashed by patriarchy or anything along the lines of "you are a weak woman". She is an ancient goddess. She likes when people "worship" her. I would say that Kedesh is primarily a goddess and secundarily a woman.

Just a stream of thoughts. Sorry if I made you feel bad or anything, I just felt confused.

item.content:encoded:
By sheer coincidence there are a lot of Mesopotamian deity SCPs that either A: take a humorous tone, or B: are a postmodern, American-Gods-esque exploration of what gods do when their worshipers are all gone. Most notably there are:

- SCP-1541 (Implied to be a Mesopotamian beer deity, presumably either Siduri or Ninkasi.)

- SCP-2270 (Nergal)

- SCP-2404-1 (Enki)

- SCP-2527-1 (I headcanon Massy as being a "robot" originally controlled by the Mesopotamian gods that was later essentially jailbroken by Totleighsoft.)

- SCP-3740 (Ashur)

- SCP-3615 (Various deities that used the title "Bel"/Baal" combined into one being.)

- Kedesh-Nanaya

- The Bull of Heaven contained by the Keepers

For a while, I've thought a tale or even a canon based on those characters could be interesting, but there's like a 70% chance that if I tried to write it, it would be terrible, and I like the concept too much to waste it on something terrible. So, I've never done anything with the idea.
